method.bootstrap: 95% intervals are percentile bootstrap over the 27 held-out test **subjects** (the resampling unit is a subject, not a window). The per-entrant column is *marginal and unpaired*; the delta column is *paired*, resampling the same subject indices for both entrants (common random numbers) so the between-entrant correlation is preserved. Ranks and significance are read off the paired column only.
method.multiplicity: Holm step-down per entrant pair across the claim-eligible horizons; h = 1 is protocol-ineligible and is not in any family
method.seed_variance: Each subject's error is averaged over the seeds before resampling, so the bootstrap CI describes subject-to-subject variability at a fixed seed set and **excludes seed variance**. The seed spread is reported beside every mean; a delta smaller than the seed spread is not a result.
method.sign_convention: positive mean delta means the incumbent has the lower error
method.wilcoxon: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over test subjects, implemented in-driver (SciPy is not a repo dependency): exact enumeration for n <= 20 without ties, otherwise the tie- and continuity-corrected normal approximation, which is what the 27-subject F8 split actually uses

provenance.cross_check: at horizons where the committed reference was already kahlus_gru, mean_delta/CI/Wilcoxon p reproduce to 1e-12; holm_p may differ (family recomposition) but no significant_after_holm verdict flips
inputs: eeg_fm_benchmark.json (per_subject_test_mse of the single committed test look)
provenance.purpose: PR #80 review item 5: paired_statistics.json references the best incumbent per horizon (tuned_ridge_ar at h=64 and h=256); this file forces kahlus_gru as the reference everywhere so kahlus-vs-rival deltas exist at all horizons
